card: Tracks the memory footprint of transactions pinned only by active block templates after they leave the node's mempool. BlockTemplateManager reference-counts template transactions, and a new IPC method getMemoryLoad() exposes the non-mempool memory load to clients. This addresses template memory management for external Stratum v2 mining providers (issue #33899) by giving clients the visibility needed to manage and destroy stale templates without changing consensus or template construction logic.
changed_since_previous: Rebased onto the merged BlockTemplateManager; moved transaction reference hashing helpers into util/hasher.h; updated GetTemplateMemoryUsage to copy references and drop the manager mutex before checking mempool presence.
evidence: Addresses issue #33899: 'Block template memory management (for IPC clients)'.
PR description links to Stratum v2 Template Provider implementation consuming the method: stratum-mining/sv2-tp#63.
problem: External IPC mining clients, such as Stratum v2 template providers, can hold block templates indefinitely. When transactions in those templates are evicted or replaced in the node's mempool, they remain pinned in memory with no visibility into how much memory they consume.

risk.why: A bug in template reference counting could leak memory or report inaccurate memory stats to IPC mining clients.

scope_notes: Extracts CTransactionRefComp and defines CTransactionRefSaltedHash in util/hasher.h so they can be reused across private broadcast and mining template management.
summary: Track the non-mempool memory footprint of transactions held by active block templates, and expose this metric to IPC clients through a new getMemoryLoad() mining interface method. Reference counting in BlockTemplateManager increments on block template creation and decrements on destruction.
